query: What signals suggest a travel expense will be declined?

per_column.name: expense_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing entries into travel vs. hardware vs. cloud lets the analyst isolate travel expenses, the exact subject of the query. Values are well-grounded in short_description and ci text.

per_column.name: ci_asset_type
per_column.rationale: A finer typing of the CI, soundly derived from ci strings (Dell Latitude->laptop, etc.). Partially redundant with expense_category but adds a travel_item axis; moderate leverage for a travel-decline query.

per_column.name: is_miscellaneous_ci
per_column.rationale: Near-constant flag (16 of 500 true) that merely restates a bucket already present in ci_asset_type/expense_category. Little new grouping power for this query.

per_column.name: entry_origin
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes manual vs automated vs travel-report origin, a plausible signal for decline likelihood. Grounded in phrasing like 'Automated creation' vs 'Procurement'. Some inference but warranted.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: A presence flag on an existing column; missing source_id could plausibly correlate with declined/incomplete records, giving some modeling leverage. Values directly and correctly derived.

per_column.name: has_processed_date
per_column.rationale: Presence flag over processed_date (nan->False). Unprocessed entries may relate to declines, offering some signal. Directly grounded and correct.

per_column.name: expense_action_type
per_column.rationale: Action lifecycle (registration/new_procurement/tracking) derived from short_description verbs; provides a distinct grouping axis. Somewhat overlaps entry_origin but adds action semantics.

per_column.name: department_group
per_column.rationale: Original table already has a 'department' column, making this largely redundant. More concerning, values look inconsistent with source text: identical hardware-procurement rows map to different groups (Customer_Support vs Sales) with no visible basis, suggesting the mapping is not soundly grounded.

judge.rationale: Most added columns give genuine grouping/modeling axes relevant to predicting travel-expense declines (expense_category, entry_origin, presence flags, action type), and their values are largely sound readings of short_description, ci, and date fields. Weak spots: is_miscellaneous_ci is near-constant and redundant, and department_group both duplicates an existing column and shows values not clearly warranted by the source text (identical rows assigned different groups). Overall the set meets both necessary conditions at a moderate-to-good level, with department_group the main groundedness concern.
